extraction.name: VOICEASSISTANT-EVAL: BENCHMARKING AI ASSISTANTS ACROSS LISTENING, SPEAKING, AND VIEWING
extraction.description: VoiceAssistant-Eval is a comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.citeAs: VOICEASSISTANT-EVAL: BENCHMARKING AI ASSISTANTS ACROSS LISTENING, SPEAKING, AND VIEWING. Ke Wang et al. arXiv:2509.22651v1 [cs.CL] 26 Sep 2025
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Test data was collected by extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. For voice personalization evaluation, texts from RoleBench were used, and three representative audio clips per 100 distinct roles were collected. Original text instructions were replaced with synthesized speech instructions using advanced text-to-speech (TTS) models. Outputs were evaluated with UTMOS, regenerating clips with scores lower than 3.8. Synthesized audio was transcribed with Whisper and compared to original instructions, retaining only audio recordings with the lowest word error rates. A multi-stage curation process was conducted to ensure data quality and reliability.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Incomplete or inappropriate items, including cases with missing or broken audio or images, as well as instances with ill-posed questions or incorrect answers, were filtered out. Approximately 10% of candidates were removed during this stage.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Diverse visual and auditory inputs were extracted from 47 source datasets. For the Listening subset, sources included 23 audio understanding datasets (e.g., LibriSpeech, Common Voice, Clotho, AudioCaps, MusicCaps). For the Speaking subset, RoleBench was used for role profiles and question texts, and other source data came from 22 datasets (e.g., AlpacaEval, MMSU, AdvBench, VCTK). For the Viewing subset, MMMU was selected as the source dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were converted into audio using three advanced text-to-speech (TTS) models (F5TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B). Texts were preprocessed for high synthesis quality: image references were replaced with descriptive phrases, texts were rewritten using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct for TTS suitability (e.g., converting numbers/math expressions), and multiple-choice options were rephrased for readability. Generated speech was evaluated with UTMOS Strong, regenerating clips until scores surpassed 3.8. To increase speaker diversity, 300 role audio clips from the role-play task were reused as prompt audio. Synthesized audio was transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3, and samples with the lowest word error rates were selected.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A four-stage curation process was applied: (1) Deduplication: Lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance were used to flag and manually remove potential duplicate questions, resulting in 15,359 samples. (2) Validation: Incomplete or unsuitable instances, such as corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers, were excluded, discarding approximately 10% of candidates. (3) Categorization: Remaining problems were assigned to 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata. (4) Sampling: Data was sampled from categorized problems to balance the representation of different tasks, yielding 10,497 high-quality samples.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: F5TTS (Chen et al., 2024b), ChatTTS (Team, 2025), Dia-1.6B (Sung et al., 2025) for speech synthesis; UTMOS Strong (Saeki et al., 2022) for evaluating generated speech quality; Whisper-Large-v3 (Radford et al., 2022) for transcribing synthesized audio.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation code will be released to ensure reproducibility. A data governance process will be maintained for auditing and removal, with the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Speaker identity and vocal timbre are considered sensitive. The benchmark includes tasks requiring personalized voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation. Safeguards are implemented to mitigate misuse risks such as identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud, including prohibiting training models to reproduce identifiable speakers without consent, requiring consent gating and watermarking for synthetic audio, and providing safety cards describing acceptable use and risks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to push the boundaries of AI assistants, instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal models and tracking progress toward expert AI assistants. It enables research on personalization while minimizing harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics through strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may carry biases from its source data and design choices, as questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. For example, the role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts, which may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. The community is encouraged to analyze model outputs for biases or unsafe behavior and contribute additional test cases probing fairness and ethical considerations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset, though sizable (10.5K curated QA items), may be limited in diversity, with prompts and evaluations primarily in English, potentially limiting generalization to diverse linguistic settings. The range of evaluated models is limited, focusing mainly on open-source models with only one proprietary system (GPT-4o-Audio). The evaluation methodology relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring, which may introduce noise and bias. The benchmark may carry biases from its source data and design choices, potentially encoding stereotypes or omitting user personas. Gaps remain in task coverage and scenario realism, as video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are beyond its scope. The benchmark evaluates models in an offline, static manner, not capturing real-world deployment factors like latency, continuous listening, partial utterances, barge-in, or error recovery.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for benchmarking and evaluating AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing abilities. It is designed to guide the development of next-generation AI assistants and multimodal models, track progress toward expert AI assistants, and facilitate future research in this area. Usage guidelines include strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards to mitigate misuse risks like identity spoofing, harassment, and fraud. Training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent is prohibited, and downstream users are required to implement consent gating, watermarking, or traceability of synthetic audio.
